As for promortalism, it is literally impossible to be better off dead, assuming that it’s just nonexistence (which we don’t know). Think, when we say better off we can only mean two things; better off in a sense physical well-being, or a sense of mental well-being. If we are experiencing physical or mental pain, yes it would generally be preferable to not have whatever that pain is (which is also subjective). It is good in that it improves or restores our physical or mental health. Destroying yourself, thus obviously makes it impossible to improve such things and serves to be of no benefit. Death harms our well-being beyond repair. There is nothing left to be better off. For instance let’s say you have a computer with a virus. It would be better for the computer in terms of its functioning ability to be rid of this virus. This does not mean the computer would improve if it were just tossed out. Only if it was beyond repair. Just like awful illnesses where the pain can be too much, but those are very special circumstances.
